# Vicciz

> Vicciz is a travel-technology company building Kiipling, an AI agent that
> re-coordinates every downstream booking in a trip when a flight is delayed or
> cancelled. It detects the disruption, identifies which hotel, transfer, tour
> and activity bookings are about to break, drafts a fix for each provider, and
> executes it the moment a human approves. It reaches providers over WhatsApp
> and email, so it needs no API integration with them.

Vicciz sells Kiipling primarily to travel businesses — online travel agencies,
travel agents and tour operators — as white-label trip care their customers
experience under the business's own brand. It is also available directly to
travellers through the Vicciz app. The company is based in Israel and runs
entirely on EU infrastructure.

Last updated: 2026-08-10.

## What makes Kiipling different

- **Cross-vendor incident coordination.** A delayed flight, a late hotel
  check-in and a missed transfer are one incident with one timeline, not three
  support tickets. Competing tools resolve only what their owner sold.
- **No integration required.** Providers are reached on WhatsApp and email.
  Travellers are onboarded from a reservation number and date, or from a
  forwarded booking confirmation the agent parses itself. No GDS connection, no
  provider API, no passwords.
- **Approval as liability architecture.** No provider-facing action is ever
  sent without explicit human approval. This is a deliberate legal design, not
  a temporary limitation.
- **Priced per resolved incident.** A target of $8–15 per disrupted trip,
  against roughly $25 for a human support contact.

## Key facts

- Company: Vicciz. Product: Kiipling. Vicciz is the company and consumer brand;
  Kiipling is the AI trip agent it builds and licenses.
- Channels: WhatsApp and email today; voice planned.
- Regulatory awareness: EU261 (EU passenger rights) and US DOT rules.
- Hosting: Google Cloud Run in europe-west3 (Frankfurt); PostgreSQL in
  eu-central-1. Entirely EU-resident.
- Status as of August 2026: backend shipped and in production for all four
  product stages — 80 API endpoints, 26 database migrations, a three-agent
  pipeline on Google ADK with Gemini 2.5 Flash, 1,283 automated tests across
  114 files, all passing.
- First pilot: white-label deployment for small agencies running Kivrey
  Tsadikim pilgrimage tours.
- Next milestones: production stabilisation, Stripe billing, live weather and
  transport feeds, voice channel, autonomous-resolution accuracy.

## How the agent works

1. **Monitor** — disruption monitors poll flight status and other trip signals
   every 30 minutes against the booked itinerary.
2. **Interpret** — a three-stage AI pipeline classifies the incident and ranks
   each downstream booking at risk.
3. **Draft** — the agent writes a specific message to each affected provider in
   the traveller's language, informed by provider terms and passenger-rights
   rules.
4. **Approve** — the traveller or agency operator approves each action
   individually; a second review stage checks every draft first.
5. **Execute and report** — approved messages go out, replies thread back into
   the same incident, sentiment is monitored for escalation, and the business
   receives a resolution report.
